entities.name: Neo Shadaloo
entities.description:
All three factions of Neo Shadaloo appear in the World Tour mode of Street Fighter 6. Ed appears on his own, with his group having separated for the time being in order to lay low, as a different faction of Neo Shadaloo is in the process of tracking them down with the goal of instating Ed as Bison's replacement and using the power of the other members for their own means. The Bison loyalist faction of Neo Shadaloo is shown operating out of a destroyed Shadaloo base, conducting numerous experiments with Psycho Power. F.A.N.G is shown to be in regular contact with this group, and works with them to track down former Shadaloo operatives in order to rebuild the organization, though he is shown to be in conflict with JP, who heads the initiative seeking to make Ed the leader.

After his resurrection, an amnesiac M. Bison arrives at the laboratory, with the group working to regain his memories and restore both him and Shadaloo to its former glory. Vega and Balrog have also shown interest in joining with the revived Shadaloo, though the latter expresses he may consider siding with Ed's Neo Shadaloo as opposed to the M. Bison loyalist faction.

The name Neo Shadaloo first appears in reference to the faction formed by Ed and Falke during the events of Street Fighter V following Shadaloo's fall. The organization's goals and intents and their ties to the fallen Shadaloo are, according to Falke's character story, to find and help those who were victims of Shadaloo's experiments, and it has been stressed repeatedly in storylines that both Ed and Falke utterly hated Shadaloo due to both being former replacement vessels for M. Bison. As such, the group is considered to be very much against the original Shadaloo and benign in motivation.

In Street Fighter 6 however, Neo Shadaloo hired Juri to capture Bosch and recover the funds he stole to stop the Suval'hal tournament. As a result, they used Bosch for Psycho Power-related experiments so that he would represent the organization in the tournament. It's unknown what are the organization's goals and intents for this, some even speculate that they simply want to bring back Shadaloo, a goal entirely contradictory to Ed and Falke's original stated intentions. However, this appears to be the work of a web of contacts maintained by F.A.N.G; furthermore, they are unaware that JP knew their movements and manipulated their actions into unknowingly helping him reviving Shadaloo's legacy with a new face, much to F.A.N.G's dismay. F.A.N.G and his contacts move forward with plans to both covertly investigate and hinder JP's operation, and later, when M. Bison resurfaces following an imperfect rebirth, to attempt to restore Bison's memories and reinstall the original dictator as the head of Shadaloo. To this end, F.A.N.G sends out his apprentice A.K.I. and manipulates the Avatar while operating under aliases such as "Fang Fei" and "Foo". In A.K.I.'s arcade, she encounters JP and corners him in battle, having him dead to rights before choosing to let him go since her master instructed her not to use lethal force.

entities.name: Cycloids
entities.description:
The are a group of characters that appear in the Street Fighter EX series. They appear as featureless humanoids, with their moveset acting as a composite of moves from several other characters.

A blue and a red Cycloid, dubbed Cycloid Beta and Cycloid Gamma respectively, appear as bonus unlockable characters in Street Fighter EX Plus.

Another blue Cycloid appears in Street Fighter EX2 Plus as an unplayable character, acting as a dummy in the Excel Break bonus stage, where it has to be defeated by using Excel combos. If the player fails the bonus stage, the Cycloid will briefly imitate the player character's victory pose. It can also appear running in the background where the high score table is shown, if the player holds start while choosing the random select option and clears the game achieving the highest score.

A pink Cycloid that the player can beat up on also appears during the credits. Using cheat devices to play as the Cycloid reveals that it has no hitboxes and cannot hit the opponent or receive damage, unless the opponent is in Excel state. If it tries to throw the opponent, a tech hit will always occur. There is also a red Cycloid (which becomes pink in Excel mode, indicating it is the same one that appears in the credits) and a green one.

entities.name: C Tier Fighters
entities.description:
The C Tier Fighters are a group of characters that debuted in Street Fighter: Duel. They are the easiest characters that can be recruited in the game with the cost of having reduced or otherwise absent features of SSS Tier and S Tier characters. As such, they are mostly presented as fighters, thugs, soldiers, and doctors, usually with tragic pasts or ambitious goals, that lead the majority of them to be aligned with Shadaloo, S.I.N., or the Mad Gear Gang.

Akaebo (赤前坊) is Japanese member of Mad Gear who specializes in throwing molotov cocktails and explosive gas cans. Growing up in poverty, Akaebo's mother struggled to find work and feed their family. He was encouraged by his mother to study and school to ensure a better life for himself.

Baldwin (鲍德温) is an English mechanical engineer, researcher, and soldier working for S.I.N. He built his own massive mech suit equipped with a minigun and flame thrower. Inside the mech suit, he is the largest playable character in Street Fighter: Duel. Dr. Baldwin believed in the ability of machines to advance mankind, if they're perfectly designed. So unwavering is this belief that he immediately balked at the thought that his research could also harm humanity.

Bethany (贝瑟妮) is an unconventional medic and scientist who uses multicolored chemicals to heal her allies or attack her enemies. The daughter of a wealthy Englishman, she was provided pharmaceutical company after her college graduation to further he research into new prototype drugs.

entities.description:
Makoto's family consist of her late father, her brother and her grandfather.

Makoto's brother and grandfather are seen in her endings from Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike and Super Street Fighter IV. Though born in the Rindokan tradition, Makoto's brother was wise to realize his lack of interest and talent for fighting, leaving the inheritance to Makoto. He is a professional salaryman who has risen to become one of the best employees of his business, and is frequently on trips throughout Japan. Her grandfather was the previous master before her father, and eagerly watches Makoto's path as a fighter.

entities.name: Dhalsim's family
entities.description:
Dhalsim's family, who live with him in India. His wife and son also practice yoga, while his wife can't stretch like Dhalsim but their son can.

Sally is seen in Dhalsim's endings from Super Street Fighter II Turbo, Street Fighter Alpha 2, and X-Men vs. Street Fighter, and Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter, and also in the background of Dhalsim's India stages from Street Fighter Alpha 2 and Street Fighter Alpha 3. In these stages, whenever Dhalsim is participating as one of the combatants, she can be seen clapping her hands joyfully whenever her husband successfully lands an attack on his opponent, but shaking her head in disappointment whenever the opponent lands an attack on him. If he wins a round, she happily spins and jumps into the air, while if he loses a round, she falls to her knees, puts her head into her hands, and seemingly cries over his loss.

In Super Street Fighter IV, Sally is in the background of the Exciting Street Scene stage, though she won't pay any fight much mind unless her husband is participating. In Street Fighter V, she appears with Datta in the background of the Apprentice Alley stage. She is also present in the Action Card Grace from the first two SNK vs. Capcom: Card Fighters games.

entities.name: Genryusai Family
entities.description:
The Genryusai clan is the original clan that founded the Bushinryu in the 15th Century. As the Soke (宗家 main family) of the Bushin Ninja Clan, the Genryusai family has organized many of their clan's activities. This would continue up until the Meiji Restoration, where many shinobi clans struggled and even disbanded. The Bushinryu's arts became obsolete and less effective as the tradition had stagnated. It would be until the Genryusai's patriarch, and 37th generation Master would come to train Zeku, his best student and 38th Bushinryu Master, that the direction of Bushinryu would change.

After the passing of the elder Genryusai, Maki, the second daughter of the late Bushinryu Master has been seeking Guy, determined to prove his superior and become the 40th Master of the Bushinryu clan.

The elder Genryusai is the 37th master of Bushinryu and the head of the Bushinryu main lineage. He is also the master of Zeku, and assisted in the instruction of Guy. He has two daughters named Maki and Rena.

Genryusai the Elder was the 37th Master of Bushinryu and the leader of the epinomous Ninja clan. Eventually in the mid-1960s, he would marry and have two young girls; Rena and Maki, the latter who he found had the potential to be the next heir, but was too young for the role. And so he trained Zeku, a member of a cadet branch who would become the 38th leader of the clan. Genryusai hoped that Zeku would train Maki to be the next successor of the art, so that when she produced an heir, the main branch of the Bushinryu would prosper.

Julia deeply loves Guile and she seeks that he do the right thing with determination. However, she is also very understanding, and allows Guile to find Charlie, because she hopes that with this he will recover from his negative feelings, despite the pain this causes her.

entities.name: Kanzuki Family
entities.description:
The Kanzuki Family is a rich family from the Street Fighter series. The daughter Karin Kanzuki is the head of the Kanzuki Zaibatsu.

The wealthy Kanzuki family's mottos are "All you need is victory" (also interpreted as "Be the winner in everything") and, alternately, "The worst we'll ever be is the best" (a bonus short in the Street Fighter III: Ryu Final manga takes this further with "Victorious, therefore Supreme! Supreme, she is Karin Kanzuki!").

Her family's private estate covers 200 miles of land, and not only has its own geographical features, but its own climate. The Kanzukis are even wealthier than the Masters, so rich that they have their own satellites, one that is called "Red Spider-Lily" and another "killer-satellite" which is capable of unleashing a devastating laser from orbit which supposedly destroyed the Psycho Drive in Karin's ending in Street Fighter Alpha 3. Karin was given a son's upbringing because her father always wanted a male heir to his conglomerate as well as being put through harsh trials to cement her family's ideals in her head and to test her worthiness of inheriting the family fortune.

Nadeshiko is described as being more lenient and caring towards her daughter than her husband is. However, she has never made any official appearances yet. However, on her husband's official Street Fighter V bio, it is stated that Daigenjuro still loves her a lot despite her having birthed a girl instead of a boy. She also runs the household while her husband's at work in the Zaibatsu. Karin learned most of what she knows from her mom, who apparently is able to bewitch 500 men at once with a single glance.

entities.name: Masters Family
entities.description:
The is a wealthy family from the Street Fighter series. They are the heads of the Masters Hotel hospitality, hostel, and resort enterprise in the world of Street Fighter. The Masters are also known to run a charity enterprise by the name of the "Masters Foundation", with a sponsorship shown at the Osaka Finals in the tournament of Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millennium 2001.

When Ken was about twelve years old, his father, a rich hotel tycoon, thought that his son needed to learn about discipline, or his son would become a spoiled brat all of his life and try to leech onto the Masters' family fortune. In order to do so, the elder Masters sent Ken to train under his best friend, the mysterious karate master Gouken.

While he is not seen in the games, Ken's father appears in Street Fighter II V and Street Fighter: Assassin's Fist.

In Street Fighter II V, Ken calls his father in several episodes for financial assistance. When Zoltar informs M. Bison that the one fighting Vega, Ken, is a member of a family as rich as the Rockefeller family, Shadaloo captures Ken. M. Bison contacts Mr. Masters and wants a ransom of 1 billion dollars. While he gathers the money, Masters's friend Ortega calls Guile and Charlie to assist in finding Ken. Ken's mother also has a brief appearance.

entities.name: Kenny Omega
entities.description:
Tyson Smith (born October 16, 1983), better known by the ring name Kenny Omega (Japanese: ケニー・オメガ, Hepburn: Kenī Omega), is a Canadian-born professional wrestler. He is signed to All Elite Wrestling (AEW), where he is also an executive vice president, and the reigning AEW International Champion in his first reign. Omega played Cody in his Street Fighter V character trailer, revealed Rose in the Summer Update 2020 video, and portrayed Sagat, C. Viper, Ingrid and Alex for Street Fighter 6's Season 3 trailer.

Kenny Omega has payed homage to Street Fighter throughout his wrestling career, either through ring attire, wrestling moves, or music. Omega's signature moves include You Can't Escape, a fireman's carry followed by a moonsault, named after Alex's quote when performing a Super Art, and V-Trigger, a running knee strike. During his time at DDT Pro-Wrestling, Omega used the Hadoken as a double palm strike while yelling the attack's name. At AEW Fyter Fest 2019, an event co-sponsored by fighting game event CEO, Omega and his partners The Young Bucks (Matt and Nick Jackson) dressed as Akuma, Ryu, and Ken respectively, coming out to Street Fighter II's title music.

At Tokyo Game Show 2023, Kenny Omega was approached by Capcom to film promotional material for Street Fighter 6 in cosplay. Initially, Capcom had wanted to include some of Omega's mannerisms in Alex's animations as thanks for his cooperation, however Omega offered to provide motion capture as well. The shoot took roughly eleven hours and included AEW professional wrestler [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Nakazawa Michael Nakazawa] as support.

Alex's alternate Level 2 Super Art Omega Wing Buster, performed after an OD Power Drop, features Omega's finger point taunt and V-Trigger knee strike, followed by his finisher, One-Winged Angel, a one-handed electric chair driver. During the animation, a dark burst of energy emerges from Alex's side in the shape of a wing, referencing Final Fantasy VII antagonist Sephiroth, whose theme is the namesake of the technique. The preceding OD Power Drop also references Omega's Snap Dragon Suplex. Category:Real-life people Category:Actors Category:Street fighter 6 Category:Wrestlers Category:Voice Actors Category:Grapplers

entities.name: Roman Reigns
entities.description:
Leati Joseph Anoaʻi (Samoan: [anoˈaʔi]; born May 25, 1985), better known by his ring name Roman Reigns, is an American professional wrestler, actor, and former football player. As a wrestler, he has been signed to WWE since 2010, where he performs on the Raw brand and is the current World Heavyweight Champion in his first reign. He is also the leader of The Bloodline stable. Reigns' 1,316-day reign as WWE Universal Champion is the longest reign of the title's history, the fourth longest world title reign in WWE history, and the longest championship reign recognized by the company since 1988.

After playing American college football for Georgia Tech, Anoaʻi started a professional football career with brief off-season stints with the Minnesota Vikings and Jacksonville Jaguars of the National Football League (NFL) in 2007. He played a full season for the Canadian Football League's (CFL) Edmonton Eskimos in 2008 before his release and retirement from football. A member of the Anoaʻi wrestling family, Anoaʻi was signed by WWE in 2010 and made his main roster debut under the ring name Roman Reigns in 2012 as a member of The Shield alongside Dean Ambrose and Seth Rollins; with Rollins, Reigns held the WWE Tag Team Championship once. The trio teamed together until disbanding in 2014, after which, Reigns entered singles competition.

From 2014 to 2020, WWE positioned Reigns as a heroic character and attempted to establish him as their next "face of the company", which was met with intense disapproval by audiences and critics. During this period, Reigns won numerous championships and accomplishments, including winning the WWE Championship three times, the WWE Universal Championship once,  and winning the Royal Rumble in 2015. After a hiatus, Reigns was repackaged as a villainous character between 2020 and 2024, which was generally met with acclaim by audiences and critics. Reigns then won his second Universal Championship and fourth WWE Championship, holding both simultaneously as the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship; upon losing the Undisputed title, the Universal Championship was retired with Reigns recognized as its final champion. In 2026, Reigns won the Royal Rumble match for a second time, and, at WrestleMania 42 won the World Heavyweight Championship.

Reigns has headlined numerous WWE pay-per-view and livestreaming events, including WWE's flagship event, WrestleMania, a record 11 times. Reigns holds the joint-record for most eliminations in a Survivor Series match (4) and is also WWE's 28th Triple Crown Champion and 17th Grand Slam Champion. He was also ranked at No. 1 in Pro Wrestling Illustrated's annual PWI 500 list of the top 500 singles wrestlers in 2016 and 2022, and was named Wrestler of the Year by Sports Illustrated in 2021.

entities.description:
He is a former bodybuilder that used to train in a gym in Florida. He also had a rock band experience, being good with a guitar and singing. His special move is the , which gives a big boot to the opponents.

Sometime during the Street Fighter III series, Hogen had a WWCA title match against Zangief in the Metro City Square Garden (MSG). Zangief ended up throwing Hogen into the crowd with a Double Lariat, which caused him to rampage while returning to the ring, and Sean (who was watching the match) knocked him out to avoid injury to the audience.

entities.name: Zelina Vega
entities.description:
Thea Megan Trinidad Büdgen (born December 27, 1990) is an American professional wrestler and actress of Puerto Rican descent. In Street Fighter 6 she is one of the available in-game commentators. She also cosplayed as Juri in WWE Royal Rumble 2023, at the "Women's Royal Rumble" match where she emulated some of Juri's moves.

She is currently signed to WWE, where she performs on the SmackDown brand under the ring name Zelina Vega and is a former WWE Women's Tag Team and WWE Women's United States Champion, and the winner of the 2021 Queen's Crown tournament. Trinidad is the first of just four women to hold the women's world tag team championships of both WWE and Impact Wrestling (the two others being Cassie Lee, Jessie McKay, and Chelsea Green).

Trinidad is also known for her time in Total Nonstop Action Wrestling as Rosita, where she was a one-time TNA Knockouts Tag Team Champion with Sarita, and for various independent promotions under her real name. She debuted on WWE's NXT brand in 2017 under the ring name Zelina Vega, where she predominantly served as the manager of Andrade "Cien" Almas. WWE released Trinidad in November 2020, but re-signed her less than six months later. Trinidad's ring name was changed to Queen Zelina after her Queen's Crown tournament win.

Trinidad portrayed fellow professional wrestler AJ Lee in the 2019 biographical film Fighting with My Family.

entities.name: The Stiff's Guards
entities.description:
The Stiff's Guards is the elite fighting guard of Devin Aranoc in Final Fight: Streetwise. They take after their boss with their no-nonsense approach and efficient handling of "business matters". Kyle and Cody face several of them in Vanessa's bar in the beginning of the game, where The Stiff captures Cody. Later Kyle faces them again in the Bijou Hotel, along with attack dogs and Glow Heads.

The Stiff's men are a well dressed army of goons, appearing with black, blue, brown or beige suits. Although they strongly resemble mafia gangsters but not street thugs, they usually appear unarmed and mainly use basic attacks. The exception is the beige goons. They only appear in the Bijou Hotel, and (excluding a scene) they always appear holding a Pistol.

They also appear in Guy's burning mansion and in the glow factory.

entities.name: Glade of Ninjas
entities.description:
The is a village of ninjas hidden in Japan.

The glade of ninjas is a village where both young people are trained at a ripe age in the style of "Ninjutsu" as well as sell their services. They are described as a "well known ninja village" in Rolento and Ibuki's story mode in Street Fighter X Tekken.

Lower rank ninjas presumably tend to not be able to choose their assignments. This is shown when Ibuki wasn't able to refuse her elder's orders to help Rolento locate Pandora, as well as extend her working contract with him without her knowing about it prior. Further evidence is shown in Ibuki's character story in Street Fighter V where a contract for Ibuki to work for Karin was set up without Ibuki knowing about it.

It is possible that the female youth of the village are allowed more social interaction, as shown with Ibuki and Sarai both attending a public learning institution and Yuta never seen outside of the village. This is likely due to Kunochi training differing from male Shinobi as the former emphasizes more on traditional feminine skills, such as the social skills required for espionage and deception against the other gender.
